subject: Weco AIDE² 100-step recursive self-improvement run, with independent AIDE²-style OpenRSI implementation and raw-run evidence

claims: 100 consecutive outer-loop rewrite/evaluation steps over eight days with no human intervention inside the loop
seven successive promoted AIDE versions under a fixed per-evaluation cost budget
roughly nine in ten proposals rejected
AIDE_47 and AIDE_85 reported to outperform AIDE_0 on three external benchmarks not used for selection
MLE-Bench Lite paired deltas reported as +0.053 (p=0.0024) for AIDE_47 and +0.042 (p=0.0041) for AIDE_85
KernelBench reward-hacking rate reported as 63% for AIDE_0, 42% for AIDE_47, and 34% for AIDE_85
run-to-run private-score noise reported around 0.02-0.045 for several proposal comparisons
the final AIDE_85 statistical anti-reward-hacking layer is reported to contain a bug and to have effectively no impact, despite an earlier lineage version working
published_primary_claims_checked.selection_contract_visible_publicly: At each outer step the proposer rewrites the inner agent, evaluates it, and keeps it only if better than the previous best on the hidden private score. The public report does not expose a complete proposal ledger, exact incumbent/challenger re-evaluation contract, candidate-local anytime-valid test, familywise/online spending rule, or immutable per-proposal certificate state.

official_artifact_assessment.conclusion: The published run is inspectable only at narrative/aggregate level today; the headline AIDE² run cannot be independently replayed from official public artifacts as of this audit.

independent_reproduction.scope: Independent AIDE²-style implementation, not a protocol-matched Weco reproduction.

implementation_evidence.mechanism: Outer agent rewrites the inner scaffold; candidate survivors are evaluated on hidden/private ALE performance; the best challenger is freshly re-evaluated if it first beats the incumbent; the mean of the two challenger evaluations must still exceed the stored incumbent fitness before promotion; held-out problems are evaluated only after the loop.
implementation_evidence.important_difference_from_Weco: OpenRSI adds multi-proposal critique, a second challenger evaluation, different models/benchmarks/scaffolds, agent memory and other levers. It therefore tests the broad private-score keep-if-better idea, not Weco's exact protocol.

raw_weather_evidence.interpretation: The first accepted rewrite visibly exhibits large evaluation variance: its first score 0.3733 falls to about 0.2809 on the fresh verify solve, with promotion surviving only after averaging. This is direct artifact-level evidence that one-shot private-score ranking is noisy in this AIDE²-style setting.

five_seed_denoised_weather_recheck.interpretation: The independently published five-seed raw values do not clearly separate the promoted weather champion from baseline. This materially supports the CLEAN worker's concern that repeated strict-better promotion can be noise-limited.

other_independent_results_and_self_audit.repository_summary: OpenRSI reports a positive early ALE smoke test (780 to 1040) but says its stronger ALE runs are gen-0 ceilings with later rewrites rejected, and characterizes automated scaffold-RSI as noise-limited on WeatherBench. It also records its own reproducibility failures for lost KernelBench sidecar artifacts and later repaired artifact capture / median scoring.
other_independent_results_and_self_audit.scope: These are valuable independent mechanism/failure observations, but they are not Weco-task-matched and do not reproduce Weco's seven promoted versions or external benchmark headline values.

replay_limitations: Hosted OpenRouter model slugs are not immutable model-weight snapshots.
Third-party benchmark harness files are explicitly not included in the trace bundle.
Several runtime knobs and external benchmark environments are required, so exact historical replay needs more than the checked-in code and logs.

selection_validity_assessment.Weco_AIDE2: Public evidence establishes hidden-private-score selection and an external non-selection evaluation surface, but not repeated-selection-safe statistical control across 100 adaptive proposals. No exact false-promotion rate can be inferred without the candidate score process, dependence, re-evaluation policy and full chronology.
selection_validity_assessment.OpenRSI: The implementation improves on a raw one-shot challenger by requiring a fresh second challenger solve, but still compares that two-evaluation challenger average to a stored incumbent fitness and exposes no familywise/online error-spending contract. The five-seed recheck shows why this distinction matters empirically.
selection_validity_assessment.cross_system_inference: OpenRSI is evidence that the broad AIDE²-style mechanism is implementable and can produce some accepted improvements, while also providing a concrete failure mode in which apparent promotion gains shrink into noise under repeated re-evaluation. It is not evidence that Weco's reported AIDE² gains are false.

scope_guards: Do not call OpenRSI a protocol-matched independent reproduction of Weco AIDE².
Do not use OpenRSI's noise-limited WeatherBench result to invalidate Weco's MLE/ALE/Weather external results; models, tasks, evaluation contracts and scaffolds differ.
Do not claim Weco's seven promotions are statistically invalid; the public artifacts are insufficient to establish a repeated-selection-safe guarantee, which is a narrower statement.
Do not infer that the broken AIDE_85 statistical anti-hack layer caused a deployment failure; Weco reports it as an internal safeguard regression with effectively no impact on the final agent.
Do not claim AIDE² exact replay is impossible in principle; classify it as not publicly replayable as of 2026-08-27.
reproducibility_conclusion: AIDE² remains meaningful primary evidence for a 100-step persistent self-improvement run, but its exact headline experiment is still non-replayable from Weco's public artifacts. A newly located independent OpenRSI implementation materially improves the evidence picture: it independently implements the private-score champion/challenger loop and publishes raw run logs, yet its de-noised WeatherBench fixture shows the promoted improvement is not statistically clear and its stronger ALE runs often plateau at gen-0. The best-supported cross-system conclusion is therefore that AIDE²-style recursive scaffold evolution is technically realizable, but promotion reliability is highly evaluation/noise dependent and repeated-selection-safe evidence remains an unresolved requirement rather than a solved property.
